title: Intake acceptance matrix and owner roster
content:
Purpose
-----
This doc proposes a compact intake acceptance matrix and a clear owner roster to speed decisions on new model additions to Redwood's serving catalog. The goal is to standardize the binary accept/canary/reject decision into measurable signals (quality, latency, cost, safety, integration effort) and assign explicit owners for each signal so intake does not stall.

Scope
-----
Covers: new open-source model variants and community weights submitted for hosted API, Dedicated candidates for benchmarking, and private deployment requests. Not covered: internal research prototypes that won't be served, or models only for offline evaluation.

How to use this doc
-------------------
1) Intake owner fills the checklist and runs baseline tests (quick_eval harness).
2) Populate the matrix with measured values from the baseline run.
3) Owners for each signal review and attach short justification and action items.
4) Triage meeting: 15 minutes to agree accept / canary / reject and next steps.

Acceptance matrix (summary)
--------------------------
We reduce the intake decision to five signals. Each signal has a pass/fail threshold (or graded bucket). The final recommendation rule is: Accept if 4/5 signals PASS and no critical safety flags; Canary if 2-3 PASS or 1-2 PASS + mitigations; Reject otherwise.

Signals and thresholds
- Quality: prompt-suite accuracy and human-eval delta
  - Threshold: model must achieve >= 90% of baseline model (currently redwood-1.2) on the task-specific prompt suite, or show clear improvement on at least one critical benchmark + no >5% regression on other critical tasks.
  - Data required: standardized prompt sets (see prompts directory), 500 eval examples for classification-type tasks or 200 multi-turn chat samples.

- Latency: p99 single-request latency on target hardware
  - Threshold: hosted-latency SLO is p99 < 850ms on the reference GPU profile; for Dedicated candidates we accept up to 1.2x the baseline if there are compensating quality wins.

- Cost (inference TPS or tokens cost): cost-per-token or throughput at target batch size
  - Threshold: relative cost <= 1.5x baseline or has quantization path that yields <=1.1x with acceptable quality loss. Must provide a quantization/compile plan if initial cost is >1.5x.

- Safety / Harm signals: toxicity, hallucination, data leakage checks
  - Threshold: no high-severity safety flags (PII leakage, direct instructions for wrongdoing). Moderate flags require mitigation plan and removal of dangerous behavior via prompt filters/guardrails.

- Integration effort / infra fit: model size, KV cache behavior, KV-disk usage, shardability
  - Threshold: integration complexity must be classified as LOW/MED/HIGH and owners must confirm feasibility within a 4 week engineering spike for MED or 2 week for LOW. HIGH requires a detailed plan and exec approval.

Example intake matrix (text representation)
- Quality: 0.93 relative -> PASS (owner: Applied ML)
- Latency: p99=720ms -> PASS (owner: Serving Runtime)
- Cost: 1.4x baseline -> PASS with quant plan (owner: Optimize)
- Safety: low-medium toxicity pattern -> MITIGATE (owner: Safety & Compliance)
- Integration: new KV format, MED -> CANARY if mitigations scheduled (owner: Platform Eng)
Recommendation: Canary with canary-size 5% of traffic and rollback thresholds defined.

Owner roster and roles (proposed)
- Intake owner (point person who runs baseline): Rohan Gupta
- Quality owner (applied evals, prompt-suite): Ava Martinez
- Serving runtime/latency owner: Micah Lee
- Cost/optimize owner (quantization, batching plans): Nora Patel
- Safety & Compliance owner: Claire O'Neill
- Platform integration owner: Diego Ramos
- Release engineer (canary orchestration): Hana Kim

Checklist for intake owner (minimal runnable baseline)
1) Confirm model provenance and license (attach link and license text).
2) Run quick_eval harness with the standard prompt-suite for the model type (cli: quick_eval --model X --suite classification). Attach raw metrics.
3) Measure p50/p95/p99 on reference GPU image with 2 warmup runs. Capture batch 1 and batch 8 numbers.
4) Run cost-throughput profiling at recommended batch sizes. Include float and quantized runs if available.
5) Run automated safety scans (toxicity detector, PII scanner, known memorization checks).
6) Try basic integration: load weights into staging runtime, verify KV cache behavior for multi-turn chat.
7) Fill matrix table, tag owners, and create a 1-paragraph recommendation.

Quick regression playbook (if model is replacing an existing baseline)
1) Run primary regression suite (baseline buckets) and compute delta per-bucket.
2) If any bucket regresses >5% absolute, create a regression ticket with reproducer prompts and sample model outputs.
3) Hold a 30-min triage with Quality + Product + Applied ML to decide rollback/mitigation.
4) If rollback, mark release as failed and trigger fallback to pinned model version.

Canary and rollout guardrails
- Canary size: default 5% (configurable to 1% for high-risk categories).
- Automatic rollback triggers: error rate >2x baseline, cost >2x, quality metric drop >7% on any critical bucket, or safety alert classified as HIGH.
- Observability: per-prompt latency, per-route token cost, and sampled outputs saved for 72 hours minimum.

Prompts and prompt-suite notes
- Each intake must reference the canonical prompt-suite for the model family (links in linked_artifacts). If an intake needs a new prompt, label it with prefix intake/ and store in the prompts repo.
- Provide 10–20 human-annotated golden outputs for small-sample human eval if the model claims a new capability.

Open questions / next steps
- Does the 90% relative quality threshold make the right tradeoff for niche tasks? Suggest a slide-deck for product to sign off on varying thresholds per product vertical.
- Should cost threshold be absolute $/1k tokens or relative to baseline? Today we use relative; proposal to add an absolute floor for infra planning.
- Define a standard storage format for the matrix outputs (CSV or small JSON) so we can query rollout history.

Appendix: short template for the intake PR title and body
- PR title: intake/model-name - quick-eval + matrix
- PR body: minimal fields: model name, weights link, license, matrix snapshot (quality/latency/cost/safety/integration), owners, recommendation (accept/canary/reject), required mitigations, suggested canary size, earliest rollout date.

Contact for questions: rohan.g@redwood.ai
